headline: Recommended Planning Board approval of nine sign applications, including 30 Manchester Street's master sign plan with conditions.
summary: Nine sign applications were reviewed, and each was recommended for Planning Board approval. All votes passed unanimously. The 30 Manchester Street master sign plan was recommended with conditions on backgrounds, messaging, and the "Market & Deli" tagline, and some of its zoning matters go to the Zoning Board of Adjustment.
decisions: Recommended that the Planning Board approve the building wall sign and projecting sign at 25 South Main Street, with a suggestion to enlarge the building wall sign; passed unanimously.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the projecting wall sign at 15 North State Street with a condition for an opaque background; passed unanimously.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the three window signs at 18 North Main Street as submitted; passed unanimously.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the 30 Manchester Street master sign plan with conditions on sign backgrounds, messaging, and the Market & Deli tagline; passed unanimously.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the freestanding sign and building wall signs at 232 Loudon Road as submitted; passed unanimously.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the projecting sign at 1-5 South Main Street as submitted; passed unanimously.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the signs at 28 South Main Street with a condition to redesign the Inkzilla Tattoo sign and move it to the cast stone corner pier; passed unanimously.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the existing building wall sign at 70 Pembroke Road as submitted; passed unanimously.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the building wall sign at 8 Loudon Road, building 1, as submitted; passed unanimously.

plain_text:
City of Concord, New Hampshire 
Architectural Design Review Committee 
 September 1, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
 The Architectural Design Review Committee (ADRC) held its regular monthly meeting on September 1, 
2026, in Council Chambers, at 37 Green St, Concord, NH. 
 
Attendees: Co-Chair Elizabeth Durfee Hengen, Alternate Member Amanda Savage, Member Merle 
Thorpe, Member Claude Gentilhomme, and Member Douglas Proctor  
 
Absent:  Co-Chair Jay Doherty and Member Ron King 
 
Staff: Alec Bass, Assistant City Planner – Community Planning; Brian Tremblay, Planning and 
Zoning Inspector; and Krista Tremblay, Administrative Technician III 
 
1. Call to Order 
Co-Chair Hengen called the meeting to order at 8:32 a.m. 
 
2. Minutes – Approve meeting minutes from August 4, 2026 
Member Gentilhomme moved, seconded by Member Thorpe, to approve the meeting minutes from 
August 4, 2026, as written. All in favor. The motion passed.  
 
3. Staff Memorandum 
4. Sign Applications 
4.1 Yamas Greek Eatery, on behalf of Yamas Greek Eatery and The Draft, LLC, requests architectural design 
review approvals for a 16-square-foot, externally illuminated existing non-permitted building wall sign 
(SP-0767-2026) and a new 1.77-square-foot non-illuminated projecting sign (SP-0792-2026) at 25 South 
Main Street in the Central Business Performance (CBP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0179) (2026-047) 
 
Kosta Alexandropoulus (25 S Main St, Concord) is present to represent this application. Mr. 
Alexandropoulus stated at the last meeting it was recommended to remove the sign at the corner and 
replace with something that they can see more brick. Mr. Alexandropoulus has ordered a sign two feet in 
diameter. Mr. Alexandropoulus is asking for a blade sign and there is an existing bracket there.  
 
Co-Chair Hengen stated when they looked at the corner sign on the building and asked to be reduced in 
size.  
 
Member Proctor stated at the last time they were thinking if you have the corner sign that you do not need 
the blade sign.  
 
Mr. Alexandropoulus stated you definitely need the corner sign for visibility.  
 
Co-Chair Hengen noted the corner sign can be larger as right now it appears there is 14 inches and they 
agreed to having 8 inches of brick.  
Co-Chair Hengen made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted with the proposed sign revisions, to both the building and projecting sign, as submitted, 
with the suggestion that the building wall sign could be increased in size to allow for 8-inches of 
brick exposed from the adjacent pilasters. Member Savage seconded. All in favor. The motion passed 
unanimously. 
4.2 Granite YMCA, requests an architectural design review approval for a new 18.76-square-foot internally 
illuminated projecting wall sign (SP-0822-2026), to replace an existing non-permitted internally 
illuminated projecting wall sign at 15 North State Street in the Civic Performance (CVP) District. (PL-
ADR-2026-0196) (2026-077)
City of Concord, New Hampshire 
Architectural Design Review Committee 
 September 1, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
Margaret Tomas (2 Hilltop Lane, Dunbarton) and Kelly O’Hara (15 N State St, Concord) are present to 
represent this application. The blue and green in the picture was replaced. The lights in the cabinet were 
not working and when they replaced the sign they fixed the lights.  
Mr. Bass stated this site is in the civic performance district which prohibits internal illumination. Mr. Bass 
noted the internal illumination of this sign is a permitted non-conformity until it is removed. However, the 
sign itself is a new sign subject to architectural design approval.  
Member Savage suggested to have a white opaque background to only show the letter Y and the YMCA.  
Laurie Piper stated it might be hard to do with the existing structure because these are two trays that are 
printed.    
Co-Chair Hengen noted the design guidelines that require opaque background.  
Member Thorpe made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted with the condition that an opaque background be placed behind the larger white 
background in accordance with Section 5.4(c) of the Design Review Guidelines. Member Savage 
seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.3 NEOPCO Signs, on behalf of Capitol Craftsman, LLC dba Romance Jewelers, and Ciborowski 
Associates, LLC, requests architectural design review approvals for three new, 1.5-square-foot non-
illuminated window signs (SP-0852-2026, SP-0853-2026, and SP-0854-2026) at 18 North Main Street in 
the Central Business Performance (CBP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0198) (2026-078) 
Glen Schadlick (5 Crosby St, Concord) is present to represent this application. Mr. Schadlick stated due 
to the architecture of the building there is no location for a flat sign or blade sign. So, they have opaque 
vinyl signs on the windows.  
Member Gentilhomme made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Member Proctor seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.4 Sousa Signs, on behalf of The Common Man Roadside and BKP Invest 1 LLC, requests architectural 
design review approvals for 1 new 87.3-square-foot internally illuminated freestanding sign (SP-0828-
2026), 1 new 85.4-square-foot internally illuminated building wall sign (SP-0829-2026), 1 new 37.1-
square-foot internally illuminated building wall sign (SP-0830-2026), 2 new, 100.7-square-foot internally 
illuminated building wall signs (SP-0836-2026 & SP-0838-2026), 2 new, 42.9-square-foot internally 
illuminated building wall signs (SP-0837-2026 & SP-0839-2026), 3 new, 40-square-foot internally 
illuminated building wall signs (SP-0833-2026, SP-0834-2026, & SP-0835-2026), 1 new, 6.8-square-foot 
non-illuminated building wall sign, (SP-0832-2026), 1 new, 10.8-square-foot non-illuminated building 
wall sign (SP-0831-2026), and 3 new, 29.25-square-foot internally illuminated canopy signs (SP-0840-
2026, SP-0841-2026, & SP-0842-2026) at 30 Manchester Street in the Gateway Performance (GWP 
District. (PL-ADR-2026-0199) (2026-079) 
Mr. Bass stated the applicant has provided a master sign plan as a previously approved development is 
coming on line. Part of this master sign plan will require zooming relief. This will not go to Planning 
Board with any known zoning non-conformities and there are zoning applications to address that.  
Jason Gagnon (225 East Industrial Dr, Manchester) is present to represent this application. Mr. Gagnon 
the entire package is on docket to go in front of the Zoning Board. The secondary sign package has three 
of the signs in the master sign plan that fit with the zoning ordinance.  
Co-Chair Hengen asked if they are to look at the overall package and there is a portion of it that conforms 
with zoning that you want to be reviewed today.  
Mr. Gagnon responded correct. Mr. Gagnon noted the first sign will be the double-sided free-standing 
sign sitting on the entry corner with Irving, The Common Man and Market & Deli cabinets that will be 
internally illuminated. The pylon structure is a stone veneer wrap. The price changer is one of the things

that are going to the Zoning Board of Adjustment.  
Co-Chair Hengen asked if the height of the pylon complies with zoning.  
Mr. Tremblay responded yes it complies with code.  
Mr. Gagnon noted for the store front main entrance will be two overhead wall signs by the peak and each 
image is considered one sign that will be internally illuminated. Below the entry doors will have an ad 
cabinet with a promotional sign box that is illuminated.  
Member Savage asked about the temporary interchangeable sign and how does it work with the design 
review guidelines.  
Mr. Tremblay stated it would be considered a permanent sign because it is made of permanent materials. 
If it was made of temporary materials it would only be good for 45 days.  
Member Savage noted that whatever they put in the A1 cabinet they need to see the print of the sign.  
Member Thorpe suggested A1, A2 and A3 should have a different level of illumination in the cabinet than 
the other signs.  
Mr. Gagnon noted a darker color background will impact the lumens. Mr. Gagnon noted B1 at the front 
entrance sign will be internally illuminated with translucent graphics. Across the front area two sets of 
dimensional non-illuminated signs. The end gable signs are bigger and the B2 and B3 signs are to the left 
and right.  
Mr. Bass stated internally illumination of signs is allowed in this district. However, the design review 
guidelines 5.4(c) “internally illumination of signs should have an opaque background. Mr. Bass noted 
normally they apply that to a white background and if there is a dark background with light copy the 
opaque background is not exercised.    
Mr. Gagnon noted for the gas canopy there are illuminated bands with the Irving channel letters. Mr. 
Gagnon noted C1 are the canopy signs. The B1 sign the gas canopy might block part of the view.  
Co-Chair Hengen asked about the signs A1, A2 and A3 that has a lot of information and on it is a QR 
code is that a functioning QR code. Co-Chair Hengen suggested to simplify the sign as it is full of 
information.  
Mr. Gagnon stated the design is a work in progress. However, with the sign being internally illuminated it 
is considered a permanent wall sign and if there were to change out the sign face and graphics it would 
require ADR approval. The secondary plan set is within the sign code of ordinance.  
Member Gentilhomme noted the lettering above the windows that is non-illuminated it is extraneous. 
Member Gentilhomme stated the lettering on the building for the market and deli is not necessary.  
Member Thorpe suggested for signs A1, A2 and A3 signs to have a beige background that would help 
solve the opaque issue.  
Co-Chair Hengen stated the overall master plan package is over signed and encourage removal of those 
that are redundant such as eliminating market and deli sign on the gables.  
Member Savage suggested for signs A1, A2 and A3 that they choose a sign to present to the Planning 
Board.  
Co-Chair Hengen suggested to have landscaping at the base of the pylon.  
Member Savage made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted with the following conditions: Signs A1,A2, and A3 shall have an dark background, which 
could be beige or ivory, or an opaque background be installed, pursuant to Section 5.4(c) of the Design 
Review Guidelines; The messaging of signs A1, A2, and A3 shall be simplified pursuant to Section 5.4(b) 
of the design review guidelines; and, the overall signage and messaging of signs B1, B2, and B3 shall be

reduced in size by removing a tagline as the overall signage on the building is overpowering the 
architectural features of the building, with the suggestion that the tag line “Market & Deli” be removed to 
satisfy this condition. Member Gentilhomme seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.5 Carolyn A. Parker Consulting and NE Signs & Awnings, on behalf of Valvoline and Loudon Automotive 
Properties LLC, requests architectural design review approvals for a new 55.24-square-foot internally 
illuminated freestanding sign  (SP-0818-2026), while maintaining existing footing, a two new 32-square-
foot internally illuminated building wall signs (SP-0819-2026 & SP-0820-2026), to replace existing 
building wall signs at 232 Loudon Road in the General Commercial (CG) District (PL-ADR-2026-0200) 
(2026-080) 
Rob McIntire (315 Derry Rd, Hudson) is present to represent this application. Mr. McIntire looking to 
reimage the store front and the freestanding sign. They will reuse the existing freestanding sign base 
format with a new pole cover and new top sign. The building sign will have new reimaging. On the side 
of the building will be a new sign. There will be new indicators on the back of the building.  
Mr. Bass noted the two building signs and pylon signs needed sign permits in our review and they way 
finding in the back does not need review.    
Member Gentilhomme made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Member Proctor seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.6 Signarama of Concord, on behalf of Live Juice and Concord Area Trust for Community Housing, 
requests an architectural design review approval for a new 7.56-square-foot non-illuminated projecting 
sign (SP-0844-2026), to replace an existing projecting sign, at 1-5 South Main Street in the Central 
Business Performance (CBP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0201) (2026-081) 
Kendra Price (249 Sheep Davis Rd, Concord) is present to represent this application. Ms. Price noted they 
are adding color to the existing sign and it will be the same size due to a logo change.  
Member Proctor made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Member Savage seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.7 Signarama of Concord, on behalf of Keeler Family Realtors, InkZilla Tattoo, and Stephen Masters, 
requests architectural design review approvals for a new 6.25-square-foot non-illuminated blade sign (SP-
0845-2026), a new 3.59-square-foot non-illuminated awning sign (SP-0849-2026), 2 new, non-
illuminated window signs measuring at 0.75-square-feet (SP-0847-2026) and 1.7-square-feet (SP-0846-
2026), and a new 3.56-square-foot non-illuminated building wall sign (SP-0848-2026) at 28 South Main 
Street in the Central Business Performance (CBP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0202) (2026-082) 
Kendra Price (249 Sheep Davis Rd, Concord) is present to represent this application. Ms. Price stated 
Keeler Family Realtors and InkZilla Tattoo are owned by the same person. They are in two separate 
suites. They wish to split the signage. They are proposing a new awning with new graphics, building sign 
and window vinyl.  
Co-Chair Hengen asked if there is a way for the hanging sign for Keeler Family and have the InkZilla 
sign be a hanging banner below it. It is confusing for someone to know where they need to enter the 
building.  
Member Porter suggested to stack the InkZilla on the concrete.    
Ms. Price stated they can put the InkZilla on the concrete.  
Co-Chair Hengen made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted with the condition that the sign for “Inkzilla Tattoo be redesigned so it is on two lines of 
script and be located below on the cast stone corner pier as the current location interferes with the 
architecture of the building. Member Savage seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.8 Joe’s Equipment Service, Inc, on behalf of ZJBV Properties LLC, requests an architectural design review

No one is present to represent this application. 
Member Gentilhomme made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Member Proctor seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
5. Building Permit Applications 
5.1 None 
6. Site Plan Applications 
6.1 None 
7. Other Business 
7.1 Any other business which may legally come before the Committee. 
7.2 Adjourn 
Co-Chair Hengen moved, seconded by Member Gentilhomme, to adjourn the meeting at 10:28 a.m. All in 
favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
 
Respectfully submitted,
